title: Anti-D Prophylaxis: Routine and Sensitising-Event Administration

evidenceAudit.scope: Rhesus D (RhD) negative pregnant woman: routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis, sensitising events, fetomaternal haemorrhage testing and postnatal anti-D, using one hospital guideline and NICE NG126.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Only one UK hospital guideline (2019, review overdue) and NICE NG126 were opened; the British Society for Haematology and RCOG guidelines were not opened.
The MKUH guideline contradicts itself: Appendix 1 (p. 17) states a minimum 500 IU at 28 weeks while sections 3.2 and 4.1 state a single 1,500 IU dose; the 1,500 IU single dose is used here.
MKUH lists no formal contraindications or adverse effects; none are inferred.

NICE NG126 advises anti-D only after surgical management of ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage, whereas MKUH gives a minimum 250 IU for medical management before 12 weeks; the two are shown side by side.
National anti-D policy in Saudi Arabia and product availability were not verified. No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynaecology guideline was opened.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: A RhD negative woman can be sensitised by RhD positive fetal red cells entering her circulation at a sensitising event or at birth. Anti-D immunoglobulin is given routinely in pregnancy and after sensitising events to all RhD negative women not known to have anti-D antibodies. Fetomaternal haemorrhage above the standard dose coverage needs extra anti-D (500 IU covers up to 4 mL fetal cells, plus 125 IU per additional mL). Women with severe thrombocytopenia or haemostasis disorders receive the same dose intravenously rather than intramuscularly.

symptoms: Vaginal bleeding, abdominal trauma, amniocentesis, miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy or termination are the events that prompt anti-D (no symptoms of sensitisation itself).
physicalSigns: Not applicable; sensitisation is detected by antibody screening.
redFlags: Sensitising event after 20 weeks: Kleihauer test needed.
Kleihauer result over 2 mL: confirm by flow cytometry.
Recurrent bleeding after 20 weeks: 500 IU at least every 6 weeks.
precipitants: RhD negative woman without anti-D antibodies.
Antepartum haemorrhage, abdominal trauma, invasive procedures, pregnancy loss.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Prophylaxis is for women not known to have anti-D antibodies; refer for specialist alloimmunisation care.

clinicalManagement.title: Routine antenatal prophylaxis
actions: Take blood group and antibody sample before the injection.
Give 1,500 IU intramuscularly in the deltoid; do not split a full 1,500 IU vial.
If missed, give at the earliest contact before labour and birth.

clinicalManagement.title: Sensitising event
actions: Before 12 weeks: minimum 250 IU in the listed situations. 12 to 20 weeks: minimum 250 IU, or 500 IU if gestation uncertain. After 20 weeks: minimum 500 IU regardless of earlier prophylaxis.
After 20 weeks do a Kleihauer test; confirm results over 2 mL by flow cytometry.

clinicalManagement.title: Delayed presentation
actions: Some protection may be given up to 10 days after the event in exceptional delay.

clinicalManagement.title: Postnatal
actions: Cord blood group; give at least 500 IU intramuscularly if the baby is RhD positive; give anti-D if baby status is unknown or the pregnancy is non-viable and the mother is RhD negative.

clinicalManagement.title: Document
actions: Document consent including that anti-D is a blood derivative, record in the notes and return the traceability tag to the blood bank.

regimens.patientGroup: RhD negative pregnant women without anti-D antibodies
adjustments: Do not split a full 1,500 IU vial.
Severe thrombocytopenia (platelets under 50,000) or haemostasis disorder: give the same dose intravenously.
monitoring: Blood group and antibody sample before the injection; record administration and traceability tag.
contraindications: No formal contraindications are listed; religious, social or medical reasons may make it unsuitable for some women.

regimens.indication: Sensitising event after 20 weeks, including recurrent bleeding
regimens.dose: Minimum 500 IU, plus 125 IU per mL of fetal cells beyond 4 mL
regimens.route: Intramuscular (intravenous in severe thrombocytopenia or haemostasis disorders)
regimens.frequency: Single dose within 72 hours; recurrent bleeding after 20 weeks: at least every 6 weeks with Kleihauer every 2 weeks
adjustments: Given regardless of earlier routine prophylaxis or prior anti-D.
A Kleihauer result over 2 mL is confirmed by flow cytometry; fetal bleeds over 4 mL may need a repeat sample at 72 hours.
monitoring: Kleihauer test after the event; flow cytometry when over 2 mL.
contraindications: No formal contraindications are listed in the source.

medicationPlan.note: Doses are from one hospital guideline; NICE NG126 differs for miscarriage and ectopic pregnancy. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: RhD negative without anti-D antibodies: 1,500 IU intramuscularly at 28 to 30 weeks (MKUH).
Minimum 250 IU for termination, medical miscarriage management, ectopic or molar pregnancy, or persistent bleeding with pain (MKUH).
Minimum 250 IU within 72 hours; 500 IU if gestation uncertain (MKUH).
Minimum 500 IU within 72 hours plus Kleihauer test (MKUH).

guidelineComparison.title: Anti-D after early pregnancy loss in the two sources

rows.parameter: Surgical management of ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage
values: Minimum 250 IU before 12 weeks; 250 IU at 12 to 20 weeks.
Minimum 250 IU for medical miscarriage management or ectopic pregnancy before 12 weeks.

values: 250 IU only for persistent bleeding with pain before 12 weeks.

teaching.scope: Rhesus D (RhD) negative pregnant woman: routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis, sensitising events, fetomaternal haemorrhage testing and postnatal anti-D, using one hospital guideline and NICE NG126.
learningObjectives: Give 1,500 IU at 28 to 30 weeks to RhD negative women.
Dose by gestation after a sensitising event and test for fetomaternal haemorrhage after 20 weeks.
pitfalls: Missing a Kleihauer test after 20 weeks.
keyPoints: 500 IU covers up to 4 mL fetal cells.
NICE and the hospital guideline differ after medical management.
